messages:
ana_sales: Hey team — ArborHealth just signed a tentative reserved capacity deal. Need to lock down throughput sizing, burst policy, and answers for their security questionnaire. Quick sync?

mike_sre: 👍 what numbers did presales use in the quote? rps / tokens / model?

ana_sales: They modeled 35–50 rps peak, avg 30 rps steady. Average prompt+response ~120 tokens. Primary model: redwood-gpt-rlhf-3.2B (quantized variant for cost). They asked for a 99.9% latency SLO 95th < 450ms.

mike_sre: Ok. rough token throughput at peak: 50 rps * 120 tokens = 6k tokens/sec -> ~518M tokens/day. That’s a lot — does that align with the committed monthly volume?

ana_sales: Their legal/finance said commitment ~12M tokens/month initially, with expected growth. They want a conservative reserved pool to avoid throttles.

julie_fin: That monthly number (12M) is far smaller than the peak run-rate above. Is presales sure they meant monthly vs daily? Need to reconcile before we size reserved GPUs.

ana_sales: Good catch — I pinged the customer, waiting for confirmation. Meanwhile we should propose two options: low-reserve (handles 95th steady) and full-reserve (handles peak bursts via reserved GPUs + burst credits).

kevin_infra: Suggested approach: produce a throughput matrix mapping rps -> GPUs for quantized 3.2B on H100 vs A100. Also include prewarm/KV-cache warmup cost and minimum preheat window. I can run perf sims tomorrow.

mike_sre: For ops runbook we need autoscale policy proposal. Minimal suggestion: min_replicas = 2 (keep some warm), target_latency_SLO = 95th < 450ms, scale_step = +1 replica per 10% queue_growth, max_replicas = 12 for reserved pool, burst to shared-hosted up to additional 8 units.

tara_prod: Can we show them a sample autoscale snippet they can review? For transparency in the contract.

kevin_infra: Sure, sample (inline):

```yaml
autoscaling_policy:
  min_replicas: 2
  max_replicas: 12
  cpu_target: 70%
  scale_cooldown_s: 30
  burst_target_pool: hosted-burst
```

mike_sre: Also call out KV cache warmup for conversational flows. If their traffic uses long prefixes, warmup time can be several hours. Suggest we run a KV-warmup simulation using their sample corpus — need 10k unique prefixes for representative hit-rate.

ana_sales: Customer said they can provide a 24-hour traffic dump (anonymized) after NDA. I'll get that.

julie_fin: Pricing note — reserved GPU monthly fee + token billing for usage above commit. We should prepare a worked example showing monthly reserved cost vs burst credit consumption for the two options. I can draft with our standard multiplier.

mike_sre: Operational blockers we need to list for the customer: KMS integration verification, VPC peering or private endpoint, SOC2 audit export, and an escalation path if we hit AZ eviction on spot-backed fallbacks.

ana_sales: They specifically asked about key management: can they bring their own KMS/HSM?

kevin_infra: Yes — Private deployment supports customer-managed KMS. For hosted dedicated we have KMS integration points; will need the key policy and a short integration window (2–3 business days) with our security team. Add that to the questionnaire response.

mike_sre: Security questionnaire answers to draft:
- Data residency: can restrict to us-east-1 or eu-west-1
- KMS: BYOK supported for Private and Dedicated via KMS policy link
- Logs: audit logs exportable to customer S3 w/ retention policy
- Pen tests: we provide pen test summary and SOC2 report on request

tara_prod: For SLAs also propose a graceful-degradation fallback plan: when reserved pool exhausted, route low-priority traffic to quantized smaller model or to hosted burst with lower SLO. Include a sample routing policy snippet.

kevin_infra: Routing policy snippet (inline):

```json
{"route_policy":"priority: reserved -> fallback: quantized-2B (80% cost saving) -> hosted-burst"}
```

mike_sre: Can someone own the presales smoke test? We should run a 2-hour synthetic at 80% of peak on staging to validate latency and KV warmup behavior.

ana_sales: I'll coordinate with customer for the traffic sample and NDA. Who wants to own the smoke test?

kevin_infra: I can run the perf sims and the smoke test if ops supports the slot. Need a day-of-week with low infra load.

mike_sre: Ops: please reserve a preheat window and ensure we have ephemeral burst capacity in case the test overloads. @deploy-bot can you schedule a deploy and tag the test job?

deploy-bot: scheduled job "arborheat-smoke" at 2026-03-26T02:00:00Z. Notified: @kevin_infra, @mike_sre.

julie_fin: Also need to lock billing terms for burst credits vs reserved. I'll send two line items: (A) monthly reserved pool (incl. maintenance) and (B) burst credits at flat rate per GPU-hour.

mike_sre: One more ops detail: prewarm KV cache — recommend preheat window = 6 hours with synthetic replay at 60% of expected token diversity. If customer only wants 1 hour preheat, call out probability of cold-miss spikes.

tara_prod: I'll prepare a one-page runbook for the customer that includes: sizing matrix, autoscale snippet, routing fallback, security bullet answers, and recommended preheat window.

ana_sales: Thanks — timeline: customer confirms monthly vs daily numbers today. Kevin to run perf sims tomorrow. Draft runbook by EOD tomorrow. Julie to prepare cost scenarios by Monday.

kevin_infra: noted. I’ll post perf sim outputs to this thread (small table + logs).

mike_sre: thumbs up. If we get the traffic dump, we can finalize the reserve recommendation.

ana_sales: cc: @julie_fin @kevin_infra @mike_sre @tara_prod — will update when customer replies. :v:
